newsitem.title: USA: Judge orders banks to disclose merger documents.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders banks to disclose merger documents.

text.p: A federal district court judge ordered two banks, with a pending merger agreement, to reveal a potential, yet silent buyer as well as turn over documents and financial statements to lawyers representing plaintiffs in a class action suit trying to halt the merger.
The class action suit was brought against The Greater New York Savings Bank and the collective of Astoria Financial Corp and Astoria Federal Savings and Loan Association.

U.S. District Court Judge, Charles Sifton ordered the two banks to give the plaintiff's lawyer's information regarding the undisclosed "other organization" that offered to buy The Greater New York Savings Bank.

This includes the contents of comunications, conversations and negotiations between the defendants and the "other organization", as well as financial and economic projections or forecasts of the banks both separately and combined.

The discovery questions posed by the judge lifted the automatic halting of discovery of evidence under the private securities litigation reform act of 1995, the plaintiff's lawyers, Weiss and Yourman and Stull, Stull & Brody, said in a statement.

Peter Cunningham, director of investor relations at Astoria Federal Savings and Loan, responding to the plaintiffs statement, told Reuters: "As in the past, this is nothing new. We still believe this suit to be without merit and will continue to move towards a September closing of the deal."
The plaintiffs lawyers, said the judge has scheduled a hearing for September 8, on their motion to preliminarily enjoin the completion of the merger agreement.
